messages.author: d2066acad687a56c
messages.subject: Timenum and Timestamp doesn't match
parts:
Hello,

I am having some trouble matching the timenum (result from running bin file through GGIR) to the timestamp (Geneactive raw data).

I converted the timenum using posixct with 1/1/1970 as origin. The converted timenum does not match with the timestamp from Geneactive raw data. What could be the issue and how can I resolve this?

see example: 

TIMENUM          Convert TIMENUM (tz= America/New_York)   TIMESTAMP (GMT-04) 
1656072085      2022-06-24 08:01:25 EDT                                    2022-06-02 23:40:24:500
1653055825      2022-05-20 10:10:25 EDT                                    2022-05-19 17:24:58:500
1654598330      2022-06-07 06:38:50 EDT                                    2022-06-06 17:22:04:000
1657884960      2022-07-15 07:36:00 EDT                                    2022-07-14 12:41:20:000
1657282150      2022-07-08 08:09:10 EDT                                    2022-07-07 09:09:51:500

Thanks for your help!

Simey

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Timenum and Timestamp doesn't match
parts:
Hi Simey,

Thanks for reporting this. Would you mind helping to investigate where the issue comes from?

  1. Are the timestamps correct in the milestone data stored in the .RData files. For example: If you load the RData file from meta/basic folder and then do print(head(M$metashort)) does that give you the timestamps you expect?
  2. Are the timestamps correct in the GGIR .csv report e.g. part2_summary.csv?
  3. Can you use function GGIRread::readGENEActiv() on one of your .bin files directly and are the resulting timestamps correct?
  4. Can you use function GENEAread::read.bin() on the same .bin file and are the resulting timestamps correct?

Thanks,

Vincent

messages.author: bec33d17cd9adcc8
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Timenum and Timestamp doesn't match
parts:
Hey Vincent and Simey

I also run into the same problem with .gt3x files. I converted TIMENUM with as.POSIXct (e.g. as.POSIXct(1626946845, tz="Europe/Brussels") and this date and time is not correct.
To answer the relevant questions you had:

  1. Are the timestamps correct in the milestone data stored in the .RData files. For example: If you load the RData file from meta/basic folder and then do print(head(M$metashort)) does that give you the timestamps you expect? YES
  2. Are the timestamps correct in the GGIR .csv report e.g. part2_summary.csv? YES
When comparing the timestamps in .RData and the ms5.outraw it seems like it is missing a day in the latter output. 
In my particular example, measurements started at 21/07/2021 18:00 and ended 29/07/2021 16:59. This is correct in .RData but ms5.outraw first timestamp is 2021-07-22 11:40:45 CEST  and the last one is "2021-07-29 06:12:15 CEST". I do not know if this has something to do with cleaning parameters? My strategy was one, and used all default cleaning settings.

Thanks for your help!
PJ

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Timenum and Timestamp doesn't match
parts:
Hi PJ,

This is because you specified save_ms5raw_without_invalid = TRUE, which removes the invalid windows (MM or WW) in the time series.

By setting save_ms5raw_without_invalid = TRUE you will get the full time series including the time segments that are not used in the part 5 reports.

Vincent
